title: Increasing the Sensitivity of Single-Coil Eddy-Current Sensors to Detect Friction Pair Wear Particles and Improving the Reliability of Online Metal Debris Detection in Oil Systems of Power Plants
content: One of the most reliable methods for assessing the condition of friction pairs in machines and mechanisms is the analysis of wear particles in lubrication systems. Inductive methods are the most commonly used among online monitoring techniques for detecting metal particles in the oil systems of power generating units. They are insensitive to the oil-air environment and allow not only detecting the presence of particles but also determining their magnetic properties, such as ferromagnetic (Fe) and non-ferromagnetic (NFe). One implementation of inductive methods uses so-called cluster single-coil eddy-current wear sensors which are multi-channel devices that process signals in parallel and have several advantages over their analogues: they offer equal sensitivity across all channels, improved information content, and increased throughput. However, like all eddy-current transducers, cluster single-coil eddy-current wear sensors have a low sensitivity to certain particles, especially NFe-particles. The article discusses two methods for improving the sensitivity of the sensors which focus on bringing the detected particles closer to the sensor’s sensitive element. Additionally, the method for enhancing the accuracy of wear particle detection by measuring the speed of particle movement with a separate device located within one of the oil passages of the sensor array is proposed.
